summary: A 90° clockwise rotation is "reverse the row order, then turn columns into rows". In Python that is `zip(*m[::-1])` (T14 — rotation, with 2D lists).

blocks.title: Read the matrix
blocks.text: N, then the header `Enter the matrix:` printed by the program, then N rows. We keep the values as strings — we only move them, and they print the same.

blocks.title: Rotate
blocks.text: `m[::-1]` puts the bottom row first. `zip(*…)` then takes the first item of every row as the new first row, the second items as the second row, and so on. `zip` gives tuples, so `list(row)` turns each into a list.

blocks.title: Print the result
blocks.text: Print the `Rotated:` header, then each row with `print(*row)` so the values are separated by spaces with no brackets.

pitfalls: Forgetting `[::-1]` → you get the transpose, not a rotation.
